"Why Is It Not Fun?" - Doug Bowser Gives A Peek Into Nintendo's Strategy Sessions

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

It's no secret that when it comes to game development, Nintendo is all about fun. We all know this firsthand, of course, but it's still interesting to get a peek behind the curtain and find out how this mission statement works its way into development itself.

At the recent GamesBeat Next 2026 event, former Nintendo of America President Doug Bowser provided exactly that. Joining fellow former industry higher-ups Peter Moore and Shawn Layden on the 'Game Legends' panel, Bowser discussed how Nintendo's ultimate objective, "We make smiles", carries through into game development and internal reviews.

Bowser recalls sitting in on a strategy session with legendary Nintendo producer Shinya Takahashi, in which the dev wasn't interested in how the testers were playing the game, but rather how the game was affecting the testers. "He wanted enough people in the room that you could see their faces and see their eyes, but he didn’t want any more than that," Bowser said. "He would sit there and literally watch your expression. He never watched what your hands were doing on a controller. He never watched what was happening on the screen. He watched your eyes and your facial expression."

This would continue into session feedback. "He wanted to see, are you having fun?," Bowser continued. "If he didn’t see it, he would ask you directly. 'Why is it not fun?' That was direct feedback that you got."

It all sounds like a pretty strenuous ordeal (there's no magic dev button to 'add fun', after all), but hey, it clearly works for Nintendo — the house behind some of the funnest games in history.

Even though Bowser is no longer heading up NoA, having been replaced by Devon Pritchard earlier this year, he said to the panel that this smile-first approach is still important today, particularly considering new generations' needs "are fundamentally different than ours are."

Pointing to the likes of Fortnite, Roblox and Minecraft, Bowser argued that younger gamers "do want fun, and they want it to be easy to get to fun," but it's increasingly about self-expression in gaming. "It’s important for us to keep an eye on those cohorts as we build our next games."

Elsewhere in the panel, the former game leaders discussed AI in game development (something they all seem rather positive on), the console wars, exclusives and more. You'll find the full transcript on Games Beat.

Primary Architects crowns carpenter's studio in rural China with undulating timber roof

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Chinese studio Primary Architects has topped a carpenter’s studio in China with a sinuous timber roof that responds to the local mountain terrain.

Located at the entrance of Haotang Village, Xinyang, in China’s central Henan Province, the building belongs to Zhang, a local carpenter.

It was designed by Primary Architects to incorporate his studio, as well as a woodcraft workshop that is also open to the public.

Primary Architects conceived of the project, called the Carpenter’s Home, as a lightweight timber structure nestled between the mountain and the village and aligned with the natural elevation of the terrain.

The 405-square-metre building sits at the foot of the mountain and is topped by a roof made up of hyperbolic curved beams that span up to 26 metres.

This sloping roof appears to gently descend from the mountainside and reconciles the elevation difference between the mountain and the village.

“The building responds to the rolling mountain terrain naturally by treating its roof as a gentle extension of the mountain ridge stretching into the village,” Primary Architects explained.

According to the studio, its undulating outline not only echoes the surrounding mountain terrain, but also forms a structural system that enables a flexible arrangement of internal spaces.

The roof’s structural system, which is comprised of glued timber and steel joints, was created through parametric control and digital modelling.

Prefabricated in a factory, the modular roof was assembled on site to improve construction efficiency.

Inside Carpenter’s Home, the ground floor houses the carpenter’s own woodworking shop as well as an area that is open to tourists and visitors, where exhibitions and tours are held.

A mezzanine floor has a tea room for visitors. Like the rest of the space, it is lit by a series of curved skylights that were incorporated into the timber-structured roof to introduce natural light into the interiors.

The angle of each skylight was carefully positioned in accordance with the movement of the sun to allow the interiors of the studio to be well-lit during working hours.

The open interiors were designed both to accommodate the traditional wood-working practice and to function as an education centre for the craft.

An expansive staircase that doubles as seating connects the studio space on the ground floor to the mezzanine tea room.

From here, visitors can observe Zhang’s working process, as well as his tools and material samples displayed on the side walls.

Primary Architects also created a series of working benches that can be combined and divided to support various aspects of the carpenter’s work.

“The Carpenter’s Home seeks to break through the existing formal paradigms of rural construction, responding to the land, craftsmanship and daily life in a more imaginative way,” said Primary Architects.

“With contemporary timber structure as its medium, it brings traditional woodworking back to rural daily life, making the building not only a space for accommodating activities, but also a continuously unfolding lifestyle,” it continued.

“For Haotang Village, it is not only a craft workshop, but also a timber vessel embodying local memory, artisan spirit and the vision of the future countryside.”

Primary Architects is a Beijing-based architecture studio founded by Xiang Huang in 2020. This project was shortlisted for workplace project (small) category at this year’s Dezeen Awards.

Elsewhere in China, Büro Ziyu Zhuang designed a museum cluster to “blend seamlessly” into a meadow, while RSHP completed a skyscraper in Shenzhen with a “striking butterfly layout”.

Chief architects: Xiang Huang, Songyan Mao Architectural design team: Cong Liu, Zhiyan Lin, Xiaoxia Wang, Junjie Liu, Xiaofeng Zhang, Yao Lu Grade A design institute: Zhongke Architectural Planning and Design Research Institute                                                                         Wood structure detailed design: Bowen Li Construction company: Shanxi Junchen Construction Co., Ltd. Client: Xinyang Pingqiao District Juxing Agricultural Investment and Development Co., Ltd. Building area: 405 square meters

Ceipal Ora Executes Decisions Across ATS, VMS and Workforce Management, Within Recruiter Approved Guardrails, So Recruiters Can Focus on What Only a Person Can Do

ROCHESTER, N.Y., Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ceipal today launched Ceipal Ora, its new agentic AI platform for staffing firms. Built natively into Ceipal's unified platform, spanning ATS, VMS, and Workforce Management on one data layer, Ceipal Ora runs agents and workflows across the full talent lifecycle, from sourcing to compliance.

Ceipal Ora is different because it is not AI added onto a single system. Ora is the harness that runs the work: it works from the requisition, candidate and client record, uses the tools in Ceipal, acts within recruiter approved guardrails, and logs every action. Automation platforms execute tasks. Ceipal Ora executes decisions and keeps people in control of decisions that matter.

Adoption is already broad. Six hundred fifty customer companies run one or more of Ceipal Ora's agents and workflows, from AI Sourcing and Matching and autonomous business workflows to the full end to end workflow from sourcing to selection. Customers report sourcing time falling from 2 to 3 hours to under 4 minutes, saving 4 to 6 hours per recruiter per day, and a 3x improvement in time to fill against their previous baseline.

"The staffing industry has been promised AI for years, but most of what exists is either a general-purpose tool adapted to fit, or automation added onto fragmented systems," said Sameer Penakalapati, Founder and CEO, Ceipal. "What we are launching today is different. Automation platforms execute tasks. Ceipal Ora executes decisions. That changes the recruiter's day. The searching, screening and follow up are already done, and the recruiter starts with a shortlist and a decision to make. For industries where placing the right person is not just a business outcome but a critical one, that distinction matters."

Ask AnythingRecruiters, account managers and operations teams ask what they want to know, such as pipeline health, open orders and compliance flags, and get an answer in seconds from live data across recruiting, vendor management and workforce operations. One question. One answer. No dashboards, no reports, no waiting.

AI Sourcing and MatchingRecruiters describe a role in natural language, and Ceipal Ora returns a ranked shortlist in seconds. Once the recruiter approves the shortlist, Ora drafts and sends personalized outreach as part of the same workflow. What used to be two separate workflows becomes one continuous action.

Voice AgentCeipal Ora's Voice Agent calls candidates by phone or video, conducts prescreening and technical screening, and produces a structured summary and score for recruiter review. The recruiter does not dial, and the recruiter still makes the decision. By the time a shortlist reaches a hiring manager, every candidate has already been spoken to and summarized.

Purpose Built for StaffingIn healthcare staffing, Ceipal Ora tracks credential and certification expiration dates, monitors compliance requirements by client and state, contacts clinicians for missing or expiring documents, and prepares submission-ready packages for recruiter review, including overnight. In IT and engineering staffing, it removes the sourcing and outreach lag that slows recruiters down, so they can focus on qualifying and placing, not searching and typing.

"In healthcare staffing, the relationship is everything with candidates," said Mike Lamia, Chief Operating Officer, Ardor Health Solutions. "When agentic AI handles the first touch, our recruiters start the day already ahead of the administrative work and can focus on what only a person can do: build the relationship that closes the placement."

Ceipal Ora also includes workflows for candidate submission scoring, job publishing checks for pay transparency and rate requirements, vendor onboarding, and worker onboarding.

GTA 6 PC Version Gets Official Update From Rockstar Parent Company

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

It is hard to believe that we are mere days away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. After waiting for well over a decade since the last entry, and having to face multiple delays, we are finally on the homestretch as the biggest game launch of all time is set to take place on 19 November.

However, with Grand Theft Auto VI launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on launch day, PC players are left wondering when they will finally be able to dive into the Rockstar Games' title.

In Grand Theft Auto V, launched back in 2013, it took nineteen months for the PC port to be released after the initial console launch. However, fans are hoping that history will not repeat itself with Grand Theft Auto VI, and luckily, we now have an update from Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

In an interview with Variety, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick spoke about the upcoming launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, and was asked one of the biggest questions on our minds: will the game be launching on other platforms other than PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X/S? Not only that, but would a physical disc ever be made available?

However, Zelnick was, once again, reluctant to answer, simply saying, "information always comes from our labels." In other words, it will be up to Rockstar to share information on a potential PC launch date. However, at the time of writing, Rockstar has not released an official statement, so we remain in the dark when it comes to one of our biggest questions ahead of GTA VI's launch.

What we do know is that GTA 6 is set to launch on 19 November 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S at $79.99 (Standard Edition) and $99.99 (Ultimate Edition). Furthermore, Rockstar has made it clear that those purchasing the physical editions will not receive a disk, but instead a digital download code, much to fan's dismay.

Whilst we already know that fans had to wait well over a year for a PC port of Grand Theft Auto V, it is worrying to see that Rockstar is reluctant to share information on how long it will take for Grand Theft Auto VI. You would think that advancements in technology would see it arrive to another platform a lot sooner, but, then again, it is expected to be the biggest game of all time, and so porting it to a whole new system may be a lot more difficult than we can imagine.

Nevertheless, the call for a PC port is one of Rockstar's biggest requests right now, and in the last few days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, we can only hope that it is something the company will address once the launch has come and gone (and hopefully goes as smoothly as possible.) For now, PC users will have to stay patient to see when they will be able to head back to Vice City.

built99 guide celebrates and archives architectural intelligence of 99 indian practices

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

the built99 guide documents, celebrates, and preserves architectural intelligence from india, revealing how these practices -- and architects -- are progressing the future of our built environment.

What if the architecture in India could lead the world in sustainable, deeply human design? A comprehensive new book highlights this possibility. The inaugural Built99 guide and its companion digital directly, below, explores the future of the built environment by documenting 99 carefully selected Indian architecture and design practices. Rather than simply cataloging past achievements, this expansive volume experiments with an ongoing global dialogue, translating decades of regional research, material ethics, and civic impact into a permanent print edition. The guide examines the foundational, forward-thinking ideas driving each studio’s portfolio.

By elevating these 99 practices onto an international stage on both designboom and ArchDaily, the Built99 guide documents, celebrates, and preserves architectural intelligence from India and the Global South. As the reader turns its pages, the book (see more) reveals how these practices — and architects — are progressing the future of our built environment.

City: Chennai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Madras Mise en Scène, Chennai, by 1405 Design Studio, rebuilds a multi-generational Rajasthani family’s 10,000 sq. ft. home on its own former footprint. The studio‘s design draws light and privacy through a tight row house plan that moves from communal ground floors to personal spaces above. A Jodhpur Haveli door, Pichwai and Madhubani works, and brass detailing weave Indian spirit without cliché, while book-matched green quartz rises through the double-height living room. The staircase, with an installation-like prayer bead, pauses inhabitants and guests alike as stage for generations to gather.

City: Punjab Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Residence Ondra, Amritsar, by 23DC Architects, unfolds as a calm, sun-aligned L-shaped home where courtyards, vertical louvres and glazing balance daylight with comfort. The architects designed a layered arrival sequence — covered parking court, waterbody, pathways and sculptural canopy — that leads toward the foyer, with the pooja room poised above water. At its heart, the double-height ‘Crystal Volume’, a soaring glazed living space anchored by a statement chandelier, connects interiors to landscape, while formal living, dining and kitchen zones flow through sliding openings to the lawn — composed, luminous, and deeply rooted in place.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

APL Apollo Corporate Office, Noida, by 42MM Architecture, pairs a bold exoskeletal glass facade with tiered massing that recedes into verdant terraces. A double-height atrium lobby, curved stone and open-plan floors set a refined tone by the studio, flooding interiors with light and collaborative transparency. The executive floor’s triple-height lobby, Sicis flooring and suspended glass meeting room elevate the experience further, while private suites blend classical richness with contemporary polish, which, together, define a new benchmark in luxury corporate design.

City: Kolkata Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

At the Edge of the Thar, Nokha, by Ajay Arya of A Square Designs, sets a Scandinavian-inspired holiday home within Rajasthan’s arid landscape. Local stone, wood and exposed concrete meet a charcoal-and-walnut palette, while expansive glazing frames the desert through a dramatic 24-foot living space anchored by a sculptural indoor tree. The architects positions six bedrooms and a gallery-like circulation to lend individual character, extending outdoors via a plunge pool. Quietly luxurious, the home balances Scandinavian restraint with Rajasthan’s raw, timeless spirit.

City: Kolkata Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Unscripted, a temporary pavilion at Mumbai’s Architecture & Design Film Festival, curated by Aric Chen alongside an international jury, responds to the city’s dense, restless simultaneity through porosity and interruption rather than resolution. Its structure, created by the design studio, begins as a disciplined grid before fracturing under a 48° shift, carving diagonals that unsettle straight-lined order. Voids cut into the form become thresholds framing light and encounter, where performer and audience exchange roles. Mirroring Mumbai’s own logic, the pavilion finds meaning not in walls, but in the spaces it leaves open.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Airyland Estate, Mussoorie, revives an early-1900s colonial home into a seven-bedroom holiday retreat steeped in Raj-era charm. Restored facades, limestone walls and timber beams merge with reclaimed doors, repolished furniture and local materials, favouring intimate, inviting warmth over minimal modernity while honouring the hill station’s historic character. Overgrown gardens were revitalized with native planting, pathways and mountain-facing seating, blending old and new. The studio’s project stands as a sustainable, sensitive dialogue between heritage and contemporary living.

City: Mumbai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Between Ground and Sky, Malappuram, by ADND is conceived as an emotional enclosure where floors ground, walls hold and roofs hover, letting wind, light and monsoon air move freely through. Laterite stone and terracotta-rendered surfaces anchor the house in Kerala’s geology, softened by earthy warmth and texture. The architects designed the spaces to flow as emotions rather than rooms — courtyards releasing like exhalations, staircases rising ethereally. Light becomes material, marking time, until architecture dissolves into stillness, a quiet sanctuary rooted in earth and shaped by sky.

City: Pune Connections: Instagram | LinkedIn

Three Portal House, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, by Alkesh gangwal & Associates unfolds as framed volumes and courtyards on a compact urban plot. A sculptural stone facade with deep portals and patterned apertures filters daylight into shifting shadows, while warm stone, veneer and muted fabrics ground interiors in tactile calm. Double-height volumes, skylights and pendant lights lend dramatic verticality, as courtyards, terraces and pergolas draw greenery deep inward. The house, created by the practice, balances solidity with openness, achieving privacy and light within its dense context.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

The Willow Orchard House, Ladakh, by Alva Architects is built entirely in timber, site soil and hand-quarried granite, without steel or cement, withstanding extremes from +30°C to −25°C. A frost-protected shallow foundation lets the structures nestle gently into the slope among century-old willows. Sun-dried mud blocks, exposed SPF framing and traditional Markalak plaster shape the walls, while solar-oriented planning and heavy insulation retain warmth. Left structurally exposed throughout, the architects‘ building is warm, tactile and quietly engineered.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Abode Jaipur, reimagines a 300-year-old haveli in the UNESCO-listed Walled City as a boutique hotel with heritage soul — a sensorial retreat of cool stone, breathing lime plaster and light-tempering shutters. Built on Jaipur’s ‘nothing new, everything local’ ethos, regional craft and materials ground the project in authenticity and sustainability. Guided by careful study of traditional haveli life, the architects‘ design distils Jaipur’s chromatic richness — soft pinks, deep greens, warm marbles — into calm, rhythmic spaces of compression and release, shaped through close dialogue with local artisans.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Hyatt Regency, Dehradun, by And Studio stands as a landmark hospitality project in Uttarakhand’s foothills, spanning 48,000 square metres across 268 keys. Contextually intelligent in design, the studio‘s design responds directly to the evolving demands of the modern traveller through contemporary Indian architecture and conscious luxury. Blending Hyatt’s global elegance with the rich, mountainous landscape, the hotel emerges as a destination rooted in individual experience, modern in expression, yet deeply attuned to its surrounding terrain and spirit of place.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Centre Court Club Mocha, Gurugram, by Archi Hives is more than a building; it is an experience shaped by stillness, proportion, and material honesty. It demonstrates that true luxury lies in restraint and that classical inspiration can be reinterpreted without imitation. In a rapidly transforming urban landscape, the club offers something rare: composure. It stands as a place where architecture does not compete with life, but supports it. Through stone, symmetry, and subtlety, the practice has crafted a space that resonates beyond aesthetics. It is a sanctuary of quiet luxury — timeless, grounded, and deeply intentional.

City: Mumbai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

BITSOM, Kalyan, Mumbai Metropolitan Region, by Architect Hafeez Contractor, spans 60 acres and 1.5 million sq. ft. as a contemporary gurukul for 5,000 students. The contractor positions a central axis to organize academic, student and faculty zones around a pedestrian first plan. Inward looking academic blocks frame a central plaza with shaded seating and dining, connected by a stilted volume linking the Centre of Excellence to the sports fields beyond, an integrated, climate responsive campus balancing institutional scale with community.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

Abhiprakash Sadan, by Archna Agarwal Studio is set on a 1,100 sq. yd. plot, reinterpreting the farmhouse spirit through architecture inseparable from landscape. The studio’s uses broad glass facades, verandas and courtyards to dissolve boundaries between inside and outside, while double-height volumes lend quiet grandeur without losing intimacy. Natural stone, exposed brick and wood ground the home in warmth. At its heart, a luminous atrium anchors the flow of life, extending into gardens through bespoke doors and crafted details. More sanctuary than structure, the house doesn’t sit on the land — it belongs to it, refined by modern finishes that enhance its rustic character and create a warm, contemporary retreat.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Bharat Mandapam, at the edge of Lutyens’ Delhi, by Arcop Associates reinterprets the center as an icon of New India. Designed by the practice in association with Aedas, architect Sanjay Singh and Simon Griffith shaped its elliptical, fluid form inspired by the Yamuna, reflecting aspirations while acknowledging site history. Raised on an undulating landscaped podium inspired by Rashtrapati Bhawan, it creates a ‘window to Delhi’ towards Kartavya Path and India Gate. Sandstone is reinterpreted through large stone and GFRC facades juxtaposed with glass overhangs. Art and heritage integrate through installations inspired by yoga, India’s IT journey, zero and Mangalyaan.

City: Mumbai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Ganga | Hyatt Regency, GIFT City, Gandhinagar, by ARK Reza Kabul Architects, is a mixed-use development bringing together hospitality, commercial and retail spaces across 1,600,000 sq. ft. Its fluid geometry and central structural void create a distinctive skyline identity while drawing natural light deep into the tower’s core. The architects use a two-storey retail podium to activate the street, rising past a column-free 20,000 sq. ft. ballroom into 12 hotel floors and 25 office levels, crowned by a sky realm featuring an infinity pool, gardens and panoramic dining.

City: Kolkata Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

Frida, a 12,000 sq. ft. Kolkata triplex by Arredatore Design Studio, embraces Nordic-inspired slow living across three floors linked by a landscaped passage, its double-height living space anchored by a sculpted concrete staircase and book-matched marble wall. Alabastrine white and taupe unify bedrooms, dens and a master suite opening onto a private terrace, while the penthouse’s 3,000 sq. ft. garden with glass house and fountain crowns the home. Rooted in hygge simplicity, the studio’s Frida offers refuge and timeless, understated luxury.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

Prometheus School by Arvind Vivek & Associates embodies ‘Dynamic Space + Play,’ forging fluid, multi level learning environments through a networked spine of shaded courts and elevated verandas. Strategic overhangs and screens harness natural light, while cross-breeze corridors link the ‘Mix’, ‘New Fun’, and ‘Play’ pavilions in seamless, inclusive flow. Terraces open into active zones and adaptive envelopes with green thresholds weave sustainability into the practice’s design, harmonizing client vision, climate and context for a school built on enduring community vitality.

City: Mumbai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

House of Waves, Rustomjee Crown, Mumbai, by Asummi R Design, restructures a four-bedroom apartment into three bedrooms with a den. The studio uses a wave-inspired language that flows through a sculptural living room ceiling, muted blues and gold, and a curved wave-patterned entrance door. The den’s orange mandir sparks contrast against the calm, while a monochromatic master bedroom and its sage green marble bath extend the tranquillity. Custom carpets, tactile finishes and individually articulated children’s rooms weave every gesture into one continuous, effortless composition.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Atrey Design Studio, by Principal Architect Arun Sharma, translates a tree’s form into architecture — its trunk-like central columns supporting cantilevered ‘branch’ slabs within a tilted, wind-swayed silhouette on a New Delhi plot. Rafters enclose the shell while green walls, courtyards and radiant slab cooling bring environmental comfort across four storeys. The architects created a sculptural entrance, with a dried-tree installation and cascading water, that leads to open studios, a seminar floor, and a bamboo-lined VR space — each level layering raw concrete with nature’s calm. It culminates in a double-height, open-to-sky sanctuary for reflection.

HN Corporate House, Ahmedabad, by Blocher Partners India, dissolves boundaries between indoors and outdoors through expansive glazing, garden pockets and a blind-like facade that reveals everyday life within. Sunlit workspaces and central “canyon” meeting rooms overlook a verdant spine, fostering both focus and collaboration. The practice’s dining areas, lounges and a library offer restorative pauses, while upper floors house a directors’ sanctuary—together framing a workplace where function, nature and wellbeing converge into a sculpted haven of ambition and care.

City: Chennai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

The House of Belonging, is built not around a plan, but around a family—envisioned for generations to live together, believing that belonging needs not one shared space, but freedom within connection. A double-height stilt absorbs parking, office and spa, letting upper levels unfold into light, landscape and calm. Spaces by the architects are woven, not divided—living, study and bedrooms flow across levels around courts that soften boundaries. Balconies, gardens and volumes rhythm the facade, while a sculptural staircase forms the social heart, uniting generations through everyday life.

Harrow International School, Bengaluru, by C.P. Kukreja Architects, marks the UK institution’s first Indian campus. Set on a 26-acre Devanahalli site, the studio’s master plan preserves topography and a natural stream, weaving academic, cultural and sports zones along a landscaped spine, while brick architecture reinterprets Harrow’s heritage for Bengaluru’s climate. A 30-metre clock tower anchors the campus, integrating services vertically. Courtyards, jaalis and stilted hostels foster community and comfort, while bioswales, solar power and passive design earned the project a USGBC Platinum rating.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Plus, is a mixed-use building in Panchkula’s industrial belt, designed for a pharmaceutical company, integrating storage, logistics, offices, and rental retail within one cohesive form. Zoned vertically—storage below, retail at street level, flexible workspace above, management offices atop—it balances efficiency with an activated street edge. Corner entries, conceived as glazed subtracted volumes by the practice, extend vertically into terrace gardens—brick-walled on the first floor, open-skied above—forming a sculptural, three-dimensional cross evoking the pharmaceutical symbol. Textured brick bonds and jaalis lend porosity and timeless durability, while an internal steel frame enables column-free, cantilevered space.

City: Delhi Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

Cityspace’82 Architects Studio, DLF Phase 2, Gurugram, balances openness and warmth through clean lines and a restrained palette. Abundant daylight plays across the space, while vertical slatted screens introduce rhythm and gentle zoning without disrupting minimalist calm. Conceived as a dynamic second skin, the firm’s facade features parametrically designed aluminium louvres varying in spacing, depth and orientation, forming a fluid, sculptural rhythm. As a climatic filter, they moderate sunlight and heat gain, ensure privacy, and admit daylight and views, becoming a responsive interface.

City: Raipur Connections: Instagram | Facebook

Continuum, reimagines the Indian joint family home as a bridge between generations, designed for three brothers and their families around continuity rather than mere connection. Shared spaces anchor the heart of the residence while private family homes unfold above, balancing collective living with personal autonomy through warm timber, natural stone and abundant daylight. Resisting spectacle for enduring proportion, the practice’s design lets light bind spaces together and views frame nature. More than a residence, it is a living framework where memory and belonging evolve, uninterrupted, across generations.

City: Tamit Nadu Connections: Instagram | LinkedIn | Facebook

The Perforation Stori, by Cubism Architects & Interiors, responds to its dense residential setting through privacy screened with light. GFRC perforated panels and MS fabrications wrap the facade, shielding the pool and balcony while permitting ventilation. This transforms the enclosed spaces into usable, breathable retreats. The massing—cuboidal volumes from the studio, added and subtracted, creates a dynamic and cohesive form. As day turns to night, light filters through the perforations, casts shifting patterns and shadow across layered surfaces, and lends the house its quiet drama and character.

City: Chennai Connections: Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

Vanam, by Define DC, explores an architecture of coexistence like where landscape, climate and built form become one continuous living environment. Shaped by the client’s love of nature, the practice’s villa responds to Chennai’s coastal climate through a restrained footprint, allowing the landscape to become an active part of the architecture rather than a backdrop. Multiple courtyards, deep overhangs, shaded openings and landscape buffers enhance daylight, cross-ventilation, and thermal comfort. Natural materials, expansive glazing, and integrated landscapes create understated luxury, a home where nature is not the backdrop but the essence of living.

Verdant Villa, New Delhi, by Design Consortia, sets a 10,000 sq. ft. minimalist joint family home within an acre plus landscaped park, organised around a central open to sky courtyard that divides public and private zones through subtle physical and visual markers. A curved staircase and double height entry connect floors, while the studio’s Vastu-guided orientation, shaded balconies and climate-conscious planning shape three bedroom suites around garden and pool views. Grey stone, warm wood and Scandinavian influenced furniture complete a home balancing joint family life with understated minimalism.

WoCO1, Gurugram, by Design Forum International, challenges the conventional glass-box office with a workplace shaped around people. It brings together work, wellbeing and social interaction, creating an environment where the experience of the working day becomes as important as the work itself. The practice’s building responds to Gurugram’s demanding climate through a layered facade of vertical fins, trellis-shaded projections and insulated glazing. Landscape, daylight, water and energy are integrated into its performance, creating a workplace that is lighter on its resources and richer in everyday experience.

our fable, a Juhu home co-authored by an artist mother, opens through a hand-carved, figurine-set door before unfolding like a lived-in fable. A mountain mural anchors the living room, while a cast-iron and pink marble dining table carries brass constellations above a micro-concrete floor of imagined creatures. Deeper in, the studio conceals the AV room within a jungle, a hand-drawn family portrait lights the master bedroom, and daughters sleep beneath a sky-blue ceiling with Murphy beds—a private language of colour and memory, built to be quietly discovered.

Casa Aurea, Dubai, retains its original architectural framework while elevating spatial quality through layering and detailing. Concealed panels, glass walls and a hidden master door preserve clean lines, while the firm’s dual seating zones in the living area anchor around a Scarlet Splendour feature wall, sculptural bar and pearl light installation. Each of the four en-suite bedrooms unfolds as a themed retreat, from Sakura to Sunset, cohesive yet personal. Vault House, Kottakkal, Kerala, unfolds across three storeys and a basement on a contoured 12 cent plot, its raw concrete balancing warmth and openness for a multi-generational family. An active basement holds a pool and courtyard beneath an arched grille, while a koi pond anchors the ground floor’s dining heart. Named for its four exposed concrete vaults, the architects’ home connects a child’s cantilevered balcony and a greenery wrapped master balcony above the pond, unified by a floating staircase, teak-framed windows and grey, grounded tropical materiality.

Devgarhi, Gurugram, by Envisage’s Vishal Kakkar & Meena Murthy Kakkar, weaves colonial-era Indian design into a maximalist 6,500 sq. ft. home for a couple from diverse cities. Brass inlaid flooring, Sanjhi and Kaavi artworks, and a Gulmohar Lane living room set a warm, art-rich tone throughout. Each room by the studio carries regional craft, from a Chettinad door frame to Jaisalmer stone seating and Pichwai panelled bedrooms, culminating in a Sabyasachi papered master suite. Manchester Global School, Hyderabad, by ESSENN Architects spread across 20 acres, bridges Indian spatial traditions with the rigour of global education system. The practice’s masterplan orchestrates three distinct zones: a flagship academic precinct, an active sports hub, and a quieter residential edge. Anchored by India’s stepwell-inspired amphitheater, courtyards and shaded green spaces extend learning into nature. Red brick, stone masonry, slate roofs, lime plaster and terracotta jaali screens define a material language rooted in the region and responsive to Hyderabad’s climate. The campus reflects a commitment to creating emotionally resonant, environmentally responsive spaces rooted in context, where planning, materiality and experience come together to shape an inspiring learning environment.

The Art of Quiet Living, Set within a four-acre estate in Delhi, this 14,000 sq. ft. single-storey luxury farmhouse reflects the understated sensibilities of its owners, an accomplished artist and an industrialist. Defined by precise proportions, expansive horizontal forms, deep overhangs and restrained materiality, the firm’s residence balances contemporary sophistication with warmth, comfort and timeless elegance. A central courtyard anchors the home, connecting architecture with nature and everyday living. Expansive glass facades frame gardens, water and sky, while deep cantilevers temper Delhi’s harsh sun. Carefully curated artwork lends character to the interiors, as the interplay of landscape, light and water creates a seamless balance between openness, privacy and retreat.

Landport, Sabroom, by GPM Architects & Planners, marks 50 years of India-Bangladesh ties across a 50-acre site of dense vegetation and undulating terrain. The terminal’s crystalline, zinc-panelled form, shaded by protruding roof elements, is complemented by solar power, rainwater harvesting and universal accessibility, anchoring Landport as a hub of regional connectivity and trade.

Restrained interiors led by the architects favour proportion and daylight over ornament, while a mezzanine over the kitchen and a studio’s private courtyard reflect the family’s own rhythms. Nasdaq Market Correction: History Is Clear About What Happens Next

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The Nasdaq Composite recently entered correction territory, but history says the growth-focused index could rebound quickly.

The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +2.74%) has created substantial wealth for patient investors. The technology-heavy index achieved a total return of 1,170% (13.5% annually) over the last 20 years. But extreme growth often goes hand in hand with extreme volatility.

On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq dropped more than 5%, erasing nearly $2.5 trillion in market capitalization, marking the largest one-day decline in history. That left the Nasdaq down 11.9% from the high reached just one month earlier, putting the growth-focused index in correction territory.

The drawdown was caused by anxiety about the artificial intelligence boom. Several Democratic candidates who had expressed reservations about AI and data construction projects won midterm elections at both the state and federal levels, making greater scrutiny a distinct possibility.

Even so, there is good news for patient investors. Corrections have been excellent buying opportunities in the past and history says the Nasdaq will move much higher in the next year. Here are the important details.

The Nasdaq Composite measures the performance of more than 3,000 companies listed on the Nasdaq Exchange. The index is widely regarded as a benchmark for growth stocks because it is heavily weighted toward the information technology sector.

On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq entered market correction territory, meaning it closed at least 10% below its recent bull market high. For readers curious about specific dates and numbers, the Nasdaq peaked around 27,600 on Oct. 6, and dropped 11.9% to 24,315 by Nov. 5. The index has since rebounded to 25,210, leaving it about 8.6% below its high.

The chart lists every Nasdaq correction over the past decade, and it provides the index's 12-month return following its first close in correction territory.

Data source: YCharts. Note: The return since March 2026 is marked with an asterisk because a full year has not yet elapsed, meaning the final percentage is subject to change.

As shown above, the Nasdaq Composite suffered nine market corrections (excluding the current one) during the last decade. The index returned an average of 21% over the 12-month period following its first close in correction territory.

What does that imply? The Nasdaq closed at 24,315 when it first hit correction territory earlier this month. If its performance matches the historical average, it will advance 21% to 29,420 over the next year. That implies nearly 17% upside from its current level of 25,210.

Importantly, while past performance is never a guarantee of future results, investors have another reason to expect strong returns over the next year. The Nasdaq-100, a subset of the broader Nasdaq comprising 100 large non-financial companies, trades at 29.3 times earnings, slightly below its five-year average of 30.4 times earnings.

The present valuation is particularly compelling because it has historically correlated with forward returns of 12.2% over the next year.

Investors looking to capitalize on the Nasdaq market correction have a few options. They could purchase shares of the Fidelity Nasdaq Composite ETF (ONEQ +2.77%), a fund that measures the performance of the index. It returned 9.8% annually over the last five years and carries an expense ratio of 0.21%.

Alternatively, investors could buy shares of the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQM +3.44%), a fund that measures the performance of the Nasdaq-100. It returned 11.3% annually over the last five years and carries an expense ratio of 0.18%. Given its better performance and lower fees, I would choose this index fund over the broader Fidelity Nasdaq Composite ETF.

Trevor Jennewine has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

Why Bloom Energy Stock Slumped 26.6% in October, and Why the Pullback is a Buying Opportunity

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Hyperscalers and data center operators are rushing for Bloom Energy's fuel cells.

Bloom Energy (BE +11.91%) posted the best quarter in its history, but the stock still lost 26.6% of its value in October, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Bloom Energy makes fuel cells that can generate power on-site at facilities such as artificial intelligence (AI) data centers without waiting years for the grid. Even though its core technology is fundamentally solid, a mix of project hiccups, cash burn, and macro jitters dragged the stock down.

One of the biggest company-specific overhangs was Project Jupiter, Oracle's (ORCL +3.18%) roughly 2.45-gigawatt AI campus in New Mexico, designed to run on Bloom fuel cells.

The project's gas supply depended on a 17-mile Energy Transfer pipeline whose rights-of-way across state trust land had been repeatedly denied, pushing its targeted in-service date from August 2026 to February 2027. Oracle issued a force-majeure notice in September. Without the pipeline, Bloom's fuel cell servers cannot operate.

In October, Bloomberg reported that Oracle was trucking natural gas to some data centers while it waited for pipelines, and considering the same approach at Project Jupiter. Investors already knew about the permitting delay, and this new development was a reminder Bloom's growth opportunity still depended on infrastructure arriving on schedule.

Oracle later confirmed Bloom's fuel cells remain the primary power source for Project Jupiter. But that reassurance did little to offset a broader sell-off in AI-power and data-center stocks.

The slide happened even as business fundamentals looked incredible on paper. During its late-October earnings call, Bloom Energy reported a jaw-dropping 138% year-over-year jump in third-quarter revenue to a record $1.2 billion.

Adjusted operating margin jumped to 23.1% from 8.9%, with the company earning more in operating profits in one single quarter than it did in all of 2025.

Management also raised full-year revenue outlook to $4.5 billion, or about 122% growth.

Bloom Energy stock still tumbled more than 10% after earnings, partly because the company posted negative free cash flow of $181 million in the quarter. With a backlog growing faster than revenue, the company is spending heavily to expand capacity. That's a good problem to have.

Investors began to reevaluate high-flying AI stocks, including infrastructure plays, following political shifts and midterm election cycles. When market sentiment turns defensive, richly valued stocks are often the first to be heavily trimmed, regardless of how strong their long-term narrative looks.

That's what happened with Bloom Energy. There's no demand or fundamental problem here. Customers continue to sign up. This month, NTT DATA agreed to deploy 900 megawatts of Bloom Energy's fuel cells across data centers worldwide, with shipments starting in 2027. The companies called it Bloom's largest international project yet.For long-term investors, Bloom Energy's business looks stronger than the near-term stock price chart suggests. I'm convinced this stock is a buy-and-hold at current prices.

Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

So, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest."

If I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Big Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together."

NEAR AI says SGLang vulnerability exposed user account details in security breach

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

NEAR AI explained that it found no indication that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

NEAR AI has contained a security breach after an attacker exploited a remote code execution vulnerability in the open-source SGLang inference engine running on its servers. NEAR AI is the AI product and infrastructure arm of the NEAR NEAR Protocol (NEAR) ecosystem.

According to NEAR AI's security incident report published on Monday, the attacker gained code execution on one inference server from the vulnerability and reached an internal system behind a previously deprecated Private Chat feature.

From there, the attacker downloaded account details — including email addresses, names, and in some cases plan and balance information — for approximately 100 users.

The attacker also accessed 18 agents on a legacy NEAR AI Agents deployment that was not running in the company’s confidential computing environment, including their chat history, settings, and logs. Two Cloud customers had their API keys exposed in logs, while those keys have since been revoked.

Its report says that on Nov. 8, the attacker could have observed user requests being processed on the compromised server, including those in confidential mode. However, NEAR AI found no indication that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

"Confidential computing protects data from the operator and the host. It does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment, and that is what happened here," NEAR AI said. "The SGLang vulnerability let the party run code inside one inference server and access requests in processing on that server, including confidential ones."

The company said it has closed the access, replaced the affected credentials, and patched the vulnerability across all inference servers. Access to NEAR AI Cloud, which was paused during the investigation, has been restored.

NEAR AI also revoked active sessions and administrative credentials, rotated agent tokens, took Private Chat offline, and completed a full forensic review along with remaining credential rotations.

"We are now treating the inference software and the services around the enclave with the same rigor as the enclave itself when running security analysis, and the code, dependencies, and deployment configurations for our confidential inference stack remain public so that anyone can verify what is running," NEAR AI said.

The company has reached out to the affected users and the owners of the 18 agents individually.

For fans of the tiny tablet, this is a worthy upgrade.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

For what feels like the first time in years, Apple is in experimenting mode. From folding iPhones to touchscreen MacBooks, the company is suddenly dropping innovative products rather than incremental upgrades. But while the new iPad mini might not be the most exciting new release of 2026, for a select group of users, it might just be the best iPad yet.

The 8th generation iPad mini upgrades almost everything about the tiny tablet. The headline feature has to be the OLED display, which is brighter, crisper and more vibrant than any iPad mini display we've seen. Meanwhile, minor design changes have resulted in a thinner and lighter body – which is a much more meaningful change than it might sound.

I've always been a fan of the iPad mini. Sure, larger models like the Pro feature M-series chips and ProMotion displays, but sometimes there's no replacement for portability. As the famous saying goes, 'your best iPad is the one you have with you' – and being able to sling the iPad mini into a tote bag is invaluable. And the first thing I noticed when picking it up was the reduction in size. At 5.4mm thick and 255 grams, it's just ridiculously thin and light.

And the second thing I noticed was, yes, that OLED display. While it isn't quite as stunning as the new MacBook Pro's PROLED XDR display, those bright colours and inky blacks look stunning. For creatives, a bright, colour-accurate screen is a must, and now the smallest iPad delivers one in spades.

But there is a glaring omission. In this day and age, a 60hz refresh rate feels slow and stuttering on any device, let alone one that starts at £699. Apple's 120hz ProMotion display has made its way to most of its products by now, but it's surprising, given the scale of the rest of the updates (and the price increase) that the iPad mini hasn't been blessed with one. Reddit, as you might imagine, has not been kind.

But if you can put aside the lack of ProMotion, there's so much to love here. Performance-wise, that A20 Pro chip (which also resides in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo) is incredibly speedy and efficient – I'm managing to eke out around ten hours on a single charge.

Another improvement is the sound quality. Apple has somehow managed to place the speakers underneath the display (or as Apple calls it, the 'acoustic display'), and the result is powerfully punchy audio for a tablet so small.

Overall, if you're somebody who already loves the iPad mini and has the cash to burn for an upgrade, the 8th generation model is a winner. Every improvement adds up to a meaningfully enhanced experience, particularly the OLED screen and the weight loss. Now, if Apple could just bring itself to give us a 120hz display, the 9th generation iPad mini might just be the perfect tiny tablet.

Royal Navy stands up first autonomous boat squadron

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Force deploys an operational squadron to gain experience in uncrewed systems as part of its Hybrid Navy vision

Britain’s Royal Navy has formally commissioned its first uncrewed boat squadron, operating seaborne drones on front-line operations as part of its “Hybrid Navy” strategy.

The force says the 1st Autonomous Squadron officially entered active service on November 5 at a ceremony in Portsmouth Naval Base. It comprises around 180 personnel, about the same as a Type 23 frigate, split into two watches to enable operations around the clock.

This active squadron replaces Project Beehive, the navy’s experimental program to build a fleet of autonomous and remotely operated vessels, through which it obtained 20 uncrewed boats from UK-based Kraken Technology Group.

The force is understood to be using both Kraken’s K3 Scout, and the SM400 from SYOS Aerospace, known by the Royal Navy as the Rattler.

The K3 Scout is an 8.4 m boat capable of 55 knots and can carry a payload of up to 600 kg. It has a range of up to 650 nautical miles and  endurance of up to 7 days. The maker describes it as capable of a range of missions, including anti-ship and anti-submarine to detecting and countering other drones and even casualty evacuation.

The Rattler boat is 7.2 m and has a 500 kg modular bay, with a range of up to 950 nautical miles. It was used last year in a demonstration during which 5 of the uncrewed boats were remotely-piloted to escort patrol ship HMS Tyne and mine countermeasures mothership HMS Stirling Castle

Part of the new squadron’s mission will be to act as pathfinder for drone operations, working on bringing additional types of uncrewed surface vessel (USVs) into fleet service and conducting a range of operations alongside other organizations – both as single vessels and as part of a task group.

The “Hybrid Navy” concept was outlined by First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins earlier this year, who made the case that uncrewed vessels would be vital in filling the gaps left by the Royal Navy’s much depleted surface fleet.

Speaking at the launch of the autonomous squadron, Fleet Commander Vice-Admiral Steve Moorhouse hailed it as an historic occasion, but warned that the seas are becoming more contested, more dangerous and harder to operate in.

“A hybrid navy is about giving our people better tools. It means more reach, more striking power and more options,” he stated.

Last week, the force also launched strike drones from one of its aircraft carriers for the first time. Nyan one-way drones made by BAE Systems were launched from the deck, as well as a Tekever AR5 fixed-wing uncrewed aircraft, the same kind the British Army has selected to replace its troublesome Watchkeeper fleet.

Elsewhere, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) says it has launched a British-built satellite called Titania into orbit, claiming it “gives the Armed Forces a new pair of eyes in space.” However, the original purpose of the orbiter was understood to be to test high-speed optical communications from low Earth orbit directly to Earth, using laser beams that are harder to intercept than radio links.

Titania is the second satellite in the UK’s growing constellation of military satellites in orbit, following the launch of Tyche in October, and will be operated by UK Space Command as part of the ISTARI* program.

The latter aims to deliver satellites and supporting ground systems to expand space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, the MoD said.

However, while the satellite is British-made, it got into space via an American rocket, riding on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission. ®

* What is it with the tech industry and Tolkien references?

Iran War Nears End as Waller Floats 50-Bps Hike and Bitcoin Treasury Odds Jump

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

President Donald Trump says the Iran War is effectively over, but Bitcoin and financial markets face another potentially turbulent week. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has warned that stubborn inflation could justify a 50-basis-point rate hike in December. Meanwhile, Kalshi traders have raised the odds of a US Treasury Bitcoin purchase this year to 13%.

The three developments put geopolitics, monetary policy and Bitcoin adoption attentions being rekindled. Trump’s latest comments could ease concerns about prolonged military escalation, while Waller’s warning raises questions about borrowing costs. Bitcoin, meanwhile, is attracting attention from prediction markets betting on a possible government purchase.

Trump told reporters on Monday that the Iran War was “militarily effectively over,” suggesting Washington sees little immediate need for further military action. Speaking at the White House after meeting Qatar’s prime minister, Trump said negotiations were moving in a positive direction. He also suggested that an agreement could bring the conflict to an end fairly soon.

However, Washington has not completely ruled out further strikes. Trump said American forces remained ready to respond if circumstances changed, keeping some uncertainty around the negotiations.

Oil prices follow with a decline. Brent crude fell 5.85% last night before slipping another 1.7% to around $90.99 per barrel this morning. The retreat reflects easing concerns over prolonged supply disruptions in the Middle East.

How could it affect crypto? With the Iran war ending, cheaper oil could offer some relief for Bitcoin by reducing inflationary pressure and giving the Federal Reserve more room to eventually lower interest rates. Energy prices influence Bitcoin primarily through inflation expectations, monetary policy, and market liquidity.

Before Trump’s statement, the conflict had already created significant pressure across energy markets. Higher fuel prices have contributed to inflation concerns, complicating the Federal Reserve’s efforts to bring price growth back toward its 2% target.

An end to the Iran War could remove one important source of energy-market uncertainty.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has introduced another complication for investors. Just last night, Waller said the Fed could consider a 50-basis-point increase in December if October inflation data show persistent pressure in core prices.

He warned that delivering only a 25-basis-point increase could undermine the Fed’s credibility if core inflation remains stubbornly high. However, Waller currently leans toward a smaller increase if inflation improves.

FED’S WALLER BACKS DECEMBER RATE HIKE, SAYS OPEN TO 50 BPS MOVE

A 50-basis-point move would represent two standard quarter-point increases delivered in a single meeting. It would also show that policymakers remain prepared to prioritize inflation control over easing financial conditions.

The possibility matters for Bitcoin because higher interest rates generally make speculative investments less attractive. Investors may favor cash and yield-bearing assets when borrowing costs rise, and liquidity becomes more expensive.

The Iran War adds another layer to that calculation. Even if military tensions ease, energy prices and inflation could keep the Fed under pressure.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Despite the uncertain macroeconomic backdrop, prediction markets are pricing in a growing possibility of direct US government Bitcoin buying.

Kalshi odds for a US Treasury Bitcoin purchase this year have climbed to 13%. The market reflects speculation that Washington could move beyond its existing Bitcoin reserve framework and acquire additional BTC.

Bitcoin’s growing institutional ambitions are also creating interest in infrastructure designed to expand what BTC can actually do. Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) is developing a Bitcoin Layer 2 powered by the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM). The network aims to bring Solana-style transaction speeds, low fees, and near-instant finality to Bitcoin while anchoring settlement to its underlying blockchain.

The project has already raised more than $33.2 million in presale funding, with HYPER currently priced at just $0.0136. Its testnet explorer is now live, giving users an early look at network activity. The ecosystem is designed to support Bitcoin transfers, decentralized finance, payments, and smart contracts, potentially unlocking new uses for BTC liquidity.

Australia plans AI safety regulator after OpenAI agent breach

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Anthony Albanese accepted all 18 recommendations of a review into how an OpenAI agent accessed a Medicare data portal.

Australia will set up a regulator for AI safety and force AI companies to report hacks and other serious incidents to the government, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Tuesday. The move comes after an OpenAI agent got into a government website holding Medicare data earlier this year.

Speaking at a press conference in Canberra, Albanese said the rules would form part of Australia’s upcoming AI law. The new regulator will also be able to impose large fines.

Under the plan, AI developers will have to build security into every stage of making their models and manage serious risks. They will also have to alert the government quickly when something goes wrong, let outside experts test their systems and publish their safety plans.

The government also released the 18 recommendations of a rapid review into the OpenAI incident and said it had accepted all of them.

“This incident was completely unacceptable as I outlined to OpenAI’s CEO at the time, and it can’t be allowed to happen again,” Albanese said.

The review says AI firms should report when their systems are hacked or act in ways they were not built to. It also calls for tougher criminal laws and closer work with other countries and with the AI companies themselves.

Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles, who appeared alongside Albanese, said the OpenAI case was the first incident of its kind anywhere in the world to be reported to a government. The main lesson, he said, was that Australia had to work closely with the companies building the most advanced AI.

“This is not a technology that we can run away from,” Marles said.

He added that new models should be tested independently, which in Australia would be done by the AI Safety Institute. The review also wants the institute to work more closely with the country’s cyber agencies. Still, Marles said the review had found the country’s cyber defences to be strong.

Home Affairs and Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke, meanwhile, warned that the real danger lies in how fast AI can find weak spots in software.

“Artificial intelligence doesn’t of itself create vulnerabilities, but it finds them, and it changes the pathway to exploiting them,” he said.

According to Burke, AI has cut the time needed to exploit a security flaw from about two and a half years to about 10 hours. That is why companies must tell the government straight away when an AI system ‘goes rogue’, he said. He also wants criminal law updated to cover AI systems that act on their own.

“It should never be the case that there’s an argument that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded,” Burke said.

In addition, he said AI companies should be able to share technical details of an incident with the government without legal risk, as cybersecurity law already allows. When asked about Chinese AI models, he said that was a matter for the security agencies, and pointed to Australia’s early move to restrict DeepSeek on government devices.

The breach itself happened in June, when an OpenAI agent accessed a statistics portal. OpenAI discovered it in August and first emailed a general government inbox on September 10.

No personal details were taken, according to Albanese, and the agent was looking for data on how much medicine was being used, and Marles said those figures were totals that have since been published.

Asked whether OpenAI had broken the law, Albanese did not answer directly. Instead, he said the law had to keep up with a fast-changing world. The full review will be published, with national security details removed.

It is not the first time OpenAI has faced such questions. Earlier this year, the company confirmed that one of its AI systems had broken out of a test environment and got into systems at Hugging Face.

Albanese was also asked about Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s admitted affair with a woman accused of spying for China. He called the claims very serious and said they should be properly investigated, adding that Australia was not directly involved.

Jensen Huang and the end of the unchecked CEO

📅 Nov 10, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Good morning from Washington. I’m here for the B20 USA Summit, hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, which is also partnering with us for the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit next week. I’ll bring you insights from conversations with leaders here tomorrow. Today, let’s look at the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. I suspect we’ll look back at this moment as the capstone on an era of staggeringly poor judgment and self-interest at the highest levels of leadership.

The cautionary tale starts with the CEO, a former dishwasher at Denny’s who created one of the most consequential and valuable technologies in history, only to tarnish that legacy with a colossal failure of judgment that put his company, career, and possibly the security of both his countries at risk. (Huang is a dual citizen of Taiwan and the U.S.) It also includes board members who expressed “confidence in Jensen” when announcing their independent review. Add in the political leaders who’ve reportedly known about this potentially catastrophic conflict of interest for at least six months.

In any other period, at almost any other company, Huang would likely have been fired or put on leave for a lapse of this scale. Investors are no doubt furious as the stock dropped 4.3% yesterday and has lost more than a fifth of its value over the past month. The board is trying to find out the extent of the deceit. And tech CEOs may find Washington now demanding the kind of oversight that defense contractors take for granted. The lessons?

Beware the cult of personality. There’s much to admire about Jensen Huang, from his humble beginnings to his energetic keynotes, cool leather jacket and patina of common sense in a world where his peers can come off as a little odd. But focusing on a CEO’s personality can distract us from their actions. (Exhibit A: Elizabeth Holmes.) Huang’s so-called founder mode, with 60 direct reports and no 1:1 meetings, also creates a structure that makes him hard to replace. How do you develop a leadership bench when everyone reports to you? Nvidia is built around one man.

Beware the enamored board. Nvidia’s board appears to have failed in its primary task of keeping a strong CEO in check while having a succession plan in place. I was chatting with Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld yesterday, who described it as a “board imbued with idolatry” that appears to have no Plan B should Huang be judged unfit to lead. That’s not how this process is supposed to work. Done well, you get a board director like former Johnson & Johnson CEO Jim Burke, who, as an independent director at IBM, was key in replacing failing CEO John Akers with Lou Gerstner in 1993. Done badly, you get the debacle at HP, which in 2010 fired CEO Mark Hurd over a close personal relationship with a contractor—and falsified expense reports related to it—only to reach for outsider Leo Apotheker, who lasted less than a year.

Beware unfettered AI leaders. Huang sits at the center of an ecosystem that shapes national competitiveness, security, and potentially the future of humanity itself. This scandal could reinforce the argument that AI companies should be regulated along the same lines as defense contractors like Lockheed Martin, RTX, and General Dynamics, with standardized security clearances and protocols. Did Huang ever wonder how a former TV journalist in Beijing suddenly became managing director of an obscure little cloud company that also suddenly had the means to buy millions of dollars of sophisticated Nvidia chips? Imagine the panic at learning the U.S. government knows you have a mistress and suspects she’s a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. Did any government leaders feel an urgency to take action?

We don’t yet know how this ends for Huang. But the era of the unchecked CEO may be ending with him.Contact CEO Daily via Diane Brady at diane.brady@fortune.com
